tldr: Instruction files are **context Claude reads**, and *where* a file lives decides **who** gets it and **when**. `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md` is yours alone; the project `CLAUDE.md` (or `.claude/CLAUDE.md`) is shared through git; a subdirectory's `CLAUDE.md` loads when Claude works in that folder. Keep files modular with **`@import`** and split topics into **`.claude/rules/`** (path-scoped when they only matter for some files). When behaviour differs between people, **`/memory`** shows what actually loaded. AGENTS.md isn't in the exam guide — the docs say Claude reads it only when there's no CLAUDE.md, unless you import it.
mentalModel: Instruction files are notices on walls: the one on your fridge (user) only you see; the one in the office lobby (project) everyone sees; the one on a lab door (subdirectory) you see when you walk into that lab — and /memory is the walk-around that shows which notices a given person actually passed.
whatItIs:
The exam guide covers CLAUDE.md scoping and organisation in Guide §6 · TS 3.1 (pp.12–13). The Claude Code memory docs describe how files
load. AGENTS.md is docs-only (📘, not gold).

**Sub-concepts — each with its picture to remember**

| # | Sub-concept | 🧭 Mental model | Source |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | User scope `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md` | The note on your own fridge: nobody else walks into your kitchen. | ⭐ TS 3.1 · Knowledge 1–2 · pp.12–13 |
| 2 | Project scope `CLAUDE.md` / `.claude/CLAUDE.md` | The notice in the office lobby — everyone who comes in (clones) sees it. | ⭐ TS 3.1 · Knowledge 1 · pp.12–13 |
| 3 | Directory scope (subdirectory `CLAUDE.md`) | A sign on the lab door: you read it when you walk into that lab. | ⭐ TS 3.1 · Knowledge 1 · pp.12–13 |
| 4 | `@import` | A notice that says “see binder 3”: the binder is fetched and read with it — found relative to where the notice hangs. | ⭐ TS 3.1 · Knowledge 3, Skill 2 · pp.12–13 |
| 5 | `.claude/rules/` | Filing by topic instead of one thick manual — and some folders open only in the room they're about (`paths`). | ⭐ TS 3.1 · Knowledge 4, Skill 3 · pp.12–13 |
| 6 | `/memory` | A walk-around audit: which notices did this person actually pass? | ⭐ TS 3.1 · Skill 4 · pp.12–13 |
| 7 | `CLAUDE.local.md` | A sticky note on your own desk in the office — it doesn't get photocopied for others. | 📘 docs |
| 8 | AGENTS.md | The same notice written for a different visitor; Claude reads it when there's no CLAUDE.md, or when CLAUDE.md points to it. | 📘 docs (not in the guide) |

**The scopes** (docs)

| # | File | Who gets it | Committed? | Loads |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md` | only you, in every project | no | at launch |
| 2 | `./CLAUDE.md` or `./.claude/CLAUDE.md` | everyone on the project | yes | at launch |
| 3 | `./CLAUDE.local.md` | only you, in this project | no (add to `.gitignore`) | at launch |
| 4 | `sub/dir/CLAUDE.md` | everyone | yes | when Claude reads files in `sub/dir/` |
| 5 | `.claude/rules/x.md` (no `paths`) | everyone | yes | at launch |
| 6 | `.claude/rules/x.md` with `paths:` | everyone | yes | when Claude reads a matching file |
| 7 | `AGENTS.md` | everyone | yes | only if no CLAUDE.md above, or via `@AGENTS.md` |

Files **add up**; they don't override each other — ordered from the root down to the working directory. CLAUDE.md is context, not
enforcement: for something that must always happen, the docs point to hooks.
howItWorks:
1. **Team rules → project `CLAUDE.md`** (or `.claude/CLAUDE.md`), committed. **Personal preferences → `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md`**, or
   `CLAUDE.local.md` for one project.
2. **Keep the root file short** (the docs target under 200 lines). Move topics into **`.claude/rules/`** — `testing.md`,
   `api-conventions.md`, `deployment.md`.
3. **Path-scope** rules that only matter for some files (`paths: ["src/api/**"]`), so they load only there.
4. **Per package, `@import`** just the standards its maintainers chose — with paths relative to the importing file.
5. **AGENTS.md already there?** Add `@AGENTS.md` to your CLAUDE.md, or Claude won't read it once a CLAUDE.md exists.
6. **Behaviour differs between people or sessions?** Run **`/memory`** (and `/context`) to see which files actually loaded.
whereSeen:
- **Scenario 2 — Code Generation with Claude Code** (Guide §5, p.3): “CLAUDE.md configurations” for a team's workflow.
- **Scenario 4 — Developer Productivity with Claude** (Guide §5, p.4): configuring Claude Code across a codebase and its packages.
- **This workbench itself:** this repo's own CLAUDE.md is a project file; your ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md holds your personal profile.

docsRefs.title: How Claude remembers your project (CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md, rules, /memory)
Best practices for Claude Code — write an effective CLAUDE.md

grounding.text: Scopes: user ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md (personal, all projects); project ./CLAUDE.md or ./.claude/CLAUDE.md (team-shared via version control); local ./CLAUDE.local.md (personal, add to .gitignore); plus an organisation-managed policy file.
grounding.ref: memory § Choose where to put CLAUDE.md files

grounding.text: CLAUDE.md and CLAUDE.local.md in the working directory and above load at launch; files in subdirectories load on demand when Claude reads files there. All discovered files are concatenated, not overridden — ordered from the filesystem root down to the working directory.

@path imports: relative and absolute paths; relative paths resolve relative to the file containing the import, not the working directory; imports can recurse up to four hops; imports outside the project prompt for approval the first time.
.claude/rules/*.md: one topic per file; rules without `paths` frontmatter load at launch like .claude/CLAUDE.md; rules with `paths` globs load only when Claude reads matching files.
Target under 200 lines per CLAUDE.md; longer files consume more context and reduce adherence. Be specific, structured and consistent — contradictory rules may be resolved arbitrarily.
/memory lists the CLAUDE.md, CLAUDE.local.md and other memory files across user and project scopes and opens them; /context shows under Memory files which files actually loaded.
grounding.ref: memory § View and edit with /memory; Troubleshoot

grounding.text: CLAUDE.md is context, not enforced configuration; it is delivered as a user message after the system prompt, with no guarantee of strict compliance — use a hook for things that must always happen.
grounding.ref: memory § CLAUDE.md vs auto memory; Troubleshoot

grounding.text: AGENTS.md: by default Claude Code reads it only when there is no CLAUDE.md, .claude/CLAUDE.md or CLAUDE.local.md in the working directory or above; with a CLAUDE.md present, import it (@AGENTS.md) or change the Project instructions setting. Reading AGENTS.md directly needs Claude Code v2.1.277 or later.
Hierarchy: user-level ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md, project-level .claude/CLAUDE.md or root CLAUDE.md, directory-level subdirectory CLAUDE.md files.
User-level instructions apply only to that user — they are not shared with teammates through version control.
@import keeps CLAUDE.md modular (e.g. importing the standards relevant to each package); .claude/rules/ holds topic-specific rule files as an alternative to one monolithic CLAUDE.md.

Skills: diagnose hierarchy problems (a new teammate missing instructions kept at user level); @import standards per package by maintainer knowledge; split a large CLAUDE.md into .claude/rules/ topic files (testing.md, api-conventions.md, deployment.md); use /memory to see which memory files loaded.
AGENTS.md does not appear in the exam guide; this page covers it from the docs only.

The loader simplifies: the working directory is the repo root; managed files, claudeMdExcludes, --add-dir and the Project instructions setting aren't modelled; instructions are recognised by marker phrases.

.claude/rules/ organises topic-specific rule files as an alternative to one monolithic CLAUDE.md.
Diagnose hierarchy issues — e.g. a new teammate not getting instructions that live at user level.
Use @import to include just the standards each package needs, based on its maintainers' knowledge.

labIntro:
You design a repository's **instruction files** (`REPO`) and your own user file (`USER`). A **simulated** loader applies the memory docs'
rules and prints a **/memory view** for four sessions: you at the root, a teammate on a fresh clone, the teammate editing billing, and
editing src/api. Four situations are checked. Three mistakes come from the exam guide (⭐), three from the docs.

labScenarios.title: A new teammate clones the repo
labScenarios.description: They start Claude Code at the repository root. Do they receive the team's rules?

labScenarios.title: Per-package standards
labScenarios.description: Billing and web have different maintainers and standards. Each package should load only its own.

labScenarios.title: The instructions have grown large
labScenarios.description: Testing, deployment and API rules must stay in effect, with API rules only for src/api code — and no CLAUDE.md over 200 lines.

labScenarios.title: The repo already has an AGENTS.md
labScenarios.description: Other coding tools read AGENTS.md. Once the team adds a CLAUDE.md, does Claude Code still follow AGENTS.md?

variants.label: ✅ ⭐ Right scope, modular, path-scoped
variants.code:
from utils.memory_lab import simulate   # SIMULATED Claude Code memory loader (rules from the memory docs)

# Your OWN machine only - never shared through git. Personal preferences belong here.
USER = {"~/.claude/CLAUDE.md": "- I prefer short answers."}

# The repository - everything here except CLAUDE.local.md is committed and reaches every teammate.
REPO = {
    "CLAUDE.md": "\n".join([
        "# Project instructions (keep this file short - topic rules live in .claude/rules/)",
        "@AGENTS.md",                                        # the file other coding tools read, imported so Claude reads it too
        "- Run `pnpm test` before committing.",
    ]),
    "AGENTS.md": "- Use conventional commit messages.",
    ".claude/rules/testing.md": "# Testing\n- Every bug fix gets a regression test.",
    ".claude/rules/deployment.md": "# Deployment\n- Deploy only from main.",
    ".claude/rules/api-conventions.md": '---\npaths:\n  - "src/api/**"\n---\n# API conventions\n- Validate every request body.',
    # each package imports only the standards its maintainers chose (paths are relative to THIS file)
    "packages/billing/CLAUDE.md": "@../../standards/money.md\n- Billing owners review every change.",
    "packages/web/CLAUDE.md": "@../../standards/ui.md",
    "standards/money.md": "- Store money as integer cents.",
    "standards/ui.md": "- Use design-system components.",
}

simulate(REPO, USER)
variants.observe: Each lab run prints a “/memory” view for four sessions. A teammate at the root gets CLAUDE.md (with AGENTS.md imported) plus the testing and deployment rules; editing billing adds packages/billing/CLAUDE.md and standards/money.md; editing src/api adds the path-scoped API rule. Your own session also shows your ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md — the teammate's doesn't.
variants.why: Team rules live in checked-in files; personal ones in user scope; packages import only their standards with paths relative to the importing file; topics sit in .claude/rules/ with the API rule path-scoped.

        "- Run `pnpm test` before committing.",
    ]),
    "AGENTS.md": "- Use conventional commit messages.",
    # WRONG: one monolithic CLAUDE.md - every topic in one ever-growing file (appended below)
    # each package imports only the standards its maintainers chose (paths are relative to THIS file)
    "packages/billing/CLAUDE.md": "@../../standards/money.md\n- Billing owners review every change.",
    "packages/web/CLAUDE.md": "@../../standards/ui.md",

                               + [f"- detailed guideline {i}" for i in range(1, 251)])   # ...and it keeps growing

distractors.name: A · Team rule in ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md
distractors.looks: It works when I use Claude.
distractors.fails: It's on your machine only — a new teammate never gets it.

distractors.name: B · Import every standard at the root
distractors.looks: One place to see all standards.
distractors.fails: Every package loads every standard — noise and conflicts.

distractors.name: C · One monolithic CLAUDE.md
distractors.looks: Everything in one place is easy to find.
distractors.fails: Over 200 lines, lower adherence; path-specific rules load everywhere.

distractors.name: D · CLAUDE.md added, AGENTS.md not imported
distractors.fails: Only when there's no CLAUDE.md; now it's skipped.

distractors.name: E · Team rule in CLAUDE.local.md
distractors.fails: It's personal and gitignored; teammates don't have it.

distractors.name: F · Import path relative to the repo root
distractors.looks: Paths usually start at the root.
distractors.fails: Imports resolve relative to the importing file — not found.

Launch — or on matching files with `paths`

experiments: Run ✅ and read the four /memory views: which files does the teammate get that you also get, and which only you?
Run ⭐❌ A, then move the pnpm line back into REPO['CLAUDE.md'] and run again.
In ✅, remove the `paths:` block from api-conventions.md and run split_rules: where does the API rule load now?
Run ❌ F and read the “FILE NOT FOUND” line in the billing /memory view — then fix the path.

questions.q: A new developer says Claude Code ignores the team's conventions (always run the linter, always use pnpm), while the other six developers' sessions follow them. The team lead wrote these conventions into a CLAUDE.md eight months ago. The repository contains no CLAUDE.md at the root or in .claude/. What is the most likely cause?
opts: The conventions are too vaguely worded, so the model applies them inconsistently from one developer to another.
The conventions live in a user-level ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md, which is not version-controlled or shared via the repo.
The new developer's session filled its context window, so CLAUDE.md was dropped before any of the rules were read.
CLAUDE.md is read only in the first session in a repository, so the new developer must run /init to load it.
questions.explain: User-level memory (~/.claude/CLAUDE.md) applies only on the machine where it lives. It isn't in the repository, so a new teammate never receives it. The missing project file is the clue. A would give inconsistent results for everyone, not a clean split between old and new developers. C and D describe loading behaviour that doesn't exist.

questions.q: In a 40-service repository, only services/payments needs extra instructions: amounts are stored in integer pence, and every change needs an audit-log entry. When these rules sat in the root CLAUDE.md, sessions working in unrelated services started converting prices to pence. Which configuration fits best?
opts: Keep the rules in the root CLAUDE.md, under a heading saying they apply only to the payments service.
Put the rules in each payments developer's ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md, so that only they ever see the instructions.
Put the rules in a CLAUDE.md inside services/payments/, which Claude loads when working in that directory.
Create a /payments-rules slash command that developers must remember to run before any payments task.
questions.explain: A CLAUDE.md in a subdirectory applies when Claude works there, so the rules reach payments work and nothing else. A still loads them everywhere and relies on the model to respect a heading. B makes team rules personal and unshared. D depends on people remembering to run a command.

questions.q: A monorepo holds a payments package and a frontend package, maintained by different teams with their own standards documents. A single shared CLAUDE.md now holds both sets of standards, runs to 900 lines, and causes merge conflicts about twice a week. What is the most maintainable setup?
opts: Split the shared CLAUDE.md into two halves, and ask each team to edit only the half that belongs to it.
Move both teams' standards into user-level CLAUDE.md files, so each developer loads only their own team's.
Replace the standards in CLAUDE.md with a short summary of each, and link to the full documents on the wiki.
Give each package its own CLAUDE.md that @imports only the standards files its maintainers say apply.
questions.explain: Package-level CLAUDE.md files that @import the relevant standards keep each team's rules modular, owned by that team, and loaded only where they apply. A keeps one file, so both the conflicts and the loading of irrelevant rules remain. B takes team standards out of version control. C: Claude doesn't follow a wiki link, so the detail is lost.

questions.q: Two developers on the same repository get different behaviour on the same task: one session follows the API conventions and the other doesn't. They have spent 40 minutes comparing their prompts without finding a difference. What should they do first?
opts: Copy the working developer's prompt word for word, then compare the output from both sessions again.
Run /memory in both sessions to see which memory files each one has actually loaded.
Reinstall Claude Code on the second machine, so both developers run with the same default configuration.
Move the API conventions to the top of the root CLAUDE.md, so that they are harder for the model to miss.
questions.explain: /memory shows which memory files a session has loaded, which is the quickest way to find a missing or extra file. A repeats the comparison that has already failed. C is a heavy change made without a diagnosis. D edits files before knowing whether the file is loaded at all.

questions.q: A repository has an AGENTS.md that three other coding tools read. The team adds a CLAUDE.md with Claude-specific notes, and from then on Claude Code follows none of the AGENTS.md conventions. Someone proposes copying AGENTS.md's contents into CLAUDE.md. What is the cleanest fix?
opts: Copy AGENTS.md into CLAUDE.md as proposed, and add a CI check that fails whenever the two files drift apart.
Delete the new CLAUDE.md, since Claude Code falls back to reading AGENTS.md when no CLAUDE.md exists.
Import it from CLAUDE.md with an @AGENTS.md line, keeping one source of truth for every tool.
Rename AGENTS.md to CLAUDE.md, and ask the other tools' users to point their configuration at it.
questions.explain: By default Claude Code reads AGENTS.md only when there's no CLAUDE.md. With a CLAUDE.md present, the docs say to import it with @AGENTS.md. A keeps two copies that have to be kept in sync. B works, but throws away the Claude-specific notes. D breaks the other tools.

faq.a: No — per the docs, all discovered files are concatenated, ordered from the filesystem root down to the working directory. If two files contradict, Claude may pick one arbitrarily, so remove conflicts.
No. It's context delivered after the system prompt, and Claude tries to follow it. For something that must happen every time, the docs point to hooks (see D1.5).
Either is a project file (guide and docs). Rules without `paths` in .claude/rules/ load with the same priority as .claude/CLAUDE.md.
It isn't in guide v1.0. It's here because the docs describe it and real repos have it.
